chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all together from Safwan ibn Yahya, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:
I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about salat (prayer) behind the Imam: Should I recite behind him?

He عليه السلام said: As for the prayer in which the recitation is not done aloud, that has been assigned to him, so do not recite behind him. And as for the prayer in which recitation is done aloud, he has only been commanded to recite aloud so that those behind him may listen attentively; so if you hear, then listen attentively, and if you do not hear, then recite.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), specifically congregational prayer behind an Imam
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the prayer leader being followed in congregational salat
key_terms.الْقِرَاءَةِ: the recitation in salat, especially Qur'anic recitation

ai.seo_question: Should a person recite behind the Imam in congregational salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on recitation while praying behind an Imam. In silent prayers, the follower should not recite behind the Imam, while in audible prayers, the follower should remain silent if he hears the recitation, and recite if he does not hear it.
